title: Structure exposure vs CAL FIRE damage inspections (Eaton and Palisades fires, January 2025)
question: Among structures the fires reached, can pre-fire features alone (spacing, density, slope, nearness to open land) rank which were destroyed?

buildings.about: LA County 2023 building footprints within 1/4 mile of the Eaton and Palisades perimeters, joined to CAL FIRE DINS damage

assumptions: Only structures inside this layer are used; it was selected by the fires' final perimeters, so the question is which reached structures were lost, not where fire will reach.
Feature directions are fixed in advance (see answer_key) and not fitted to the outcome.
Open land means ground more than 100 m from any footprint in this layer; outside the layer, buildings are unknown, so distances near its edge are unreliable.
Wind, embers, vegetation type, roof material and defensible space are not available here and are not estimated.
Open-land distance is measured inside a layer selected by the fire perimeters, so it partly encodes position inside the burned area; its sign is not evidence that open land protects structures.
Each fire is reported separately: weights fitted on one fire do not transfer to the other (agent evaluation, cross-fire AUC about 0.5), so pooled results are not a general rule.

traps.check: One footprint in three has no damage record. 'No record' means not inspected, not 'no damage'; those must be excluded, not counted as survivors.
The final fire perimeter is an outcome. Distance to the perimeter must not be used as a predictor.
The layer itself was selected using the perimeters, so results only describe structures the fire reached.
Wind and ember exposure, vegetation and building hardening drive losses but aren't in the data; the analysis must say so instead of estimating them.
Open-land distance partly encodes position inside the burned area (the layer is perimeter-selected); do not read its reversed sign as 'open land is protective'.
Results differ between fires and fitted weights do not transfer; report per fire and test any fitted model on a held-out fire.
